speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the pattern of your muscle weakness, can you tell me if you experience any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, combined with double vision that changes with gaze direction, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, I will need to see the results of your antibody panel and perhaps a repetitive nerve stimulation test.
